questions.question: Which of these are valid reasons to split data into train/validation/test sets? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To get an unbiased final performance estimate
To tune hyperparameters without data leakage

questions.explanation: Separating data into training, validation, and test sets helps evaluate whether a machine learning model generalizes to unseen data. The training set is used to learn model parameters, while the validation set is used during development to compare models, tune hyperparameters, and detect problems such as overfitting without repeatedly using the test data. The test set is kept separate until final evaluation so that it can provide a more unbiased estimate of real-world performance. The purpose of splitting is not to reduce the total amount of available data, but to create separate datasets for training, development, and final evaluation.

questions.question: A self-driving car agent faces an unexpected obstacle. Which of these should influence its decision? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: An autonomous driving agent must make decisions using information that is relevant to safe and lawful vehicle operation. The safety of passengers, pedestrians, and other road users is a critical consideration. Traffic rules and regulations constrain which actions are acceptable, while the vehicle's current speed and dynamics determine which maneuvers can be performed safely. The color of nearby buildings would normally have no meaningful relationship to obstacle avoidance and therefore should not influence the driving decision.

questions.question: You need an AI agent that can explain its decisions to users. Which approach should you prioritize?
questions.explanation: When users need to understand why an AI system made a particular decision, interpretability and explainability should be prioritized. Interpretable models can make decision logic easier to understand directly, while explainability techniques can provide insights into the factors, features, or evidence that influenced a more complex model's output. This is especially important in high-impact applications where transparency, accountability, auditing, and user trust matter. Faster inference and larger datasets may improve other aspects of the system, but they do not by themselves make individual AI decisions understandable.
